doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Art Taylor's story that nobody wanted to follow him
summary: Brown relays that drummers avoided following Haynes at drummer nights; Haynes dislikes such events.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Another drummer who was discussing your uniqueness was Art Taylor, conducting an oral history with him. He said that there was a night with a lot of drummers – I don’t think it was the Gene Krupa event, but it was some other event where there were a lot of drummers. I think it was maybe Gretsch night or something like that. He said, whenever Roy Haynes got – nobody wanted to follow Roy Haynes. He said everybody wanted to get on the bandstand before Roy Haynes got to the gig.

I didn’t know that. But I do know of one case. Yeah, I won’t get into that. Not him, necessarily. That’s wild. I’ve never played Gretsch, so I wasn’t – they didn’t have to worry about me being on no Gretsch night.

Right. But maybe – no – I think they were hosting a battle. Was it drummer’s night or some battle? Something. There was always – a bevy of drummers would be down there. They’d say, oh shoot, I don’t want him to get on the bandstand.
